commits.message:
feat(hermes-850): implement the fetch-from-provider step for Gmail/Graph

Closes the one gap HERMES-850's own closure doc (§7) named as the real
remaining work: the connector code (normalize_gmail_message,
normalize_graph_message) and webhook endpoints existed and were tested
against sample payloads, but neither push/webhook handler actually called
out to the provider's API to fetch the message that changed -- they just
acknowledged the notification and stopped.

Gmail (app/providers/gmail/service.py):
- fetch_new_gmail_messages(notification_history_id): Pub/Sub push only
  carries the mailbox's CURRENT historyId, not a delta, so finding what
  actually changed requires calling history.list with startHistoryId set
  to the LAST historyId Hermes processed. That cursor is persisted at
  /hermes-runtime/gmail/history_cursor.json via the existing
  app.runtime.jsonl_store helpers (same mechanism app/drafts/service.py
  already uses). First-ever notification for a mailbox has no prior
  cursor -- stores it as the baseline and returns [] rather than
  guessing at history from before Hermes started watching.
- Refresh-token OAuth exchange + authenticated messages.get, using
  stdlib urllib (Request/urlopen) to match this codebase's existing
  outbound-HTTP convention (see app/providers/linkedin/service.py,
  app/providers/telegram/service.py) rather than introducing a new HTTP
  client dependency.
- Never raises: missing credentials or any API failure returns [] --
  Pub/Sub redelivers on non-2xx, so failing the whole webhook response
  would cause duplicate delivery, not recovery.

Microsoft Graph (app/providers/microsoft_graph/service.py):
- fetch_graph_message(resource): app-only (client-credentials) token
  acquisition + a direct GET of the notification's own `resource` field
  against Graph v1.0. App-only, not delegated, since there's no
  interactive user in a webhook handler -- requires the app registration
  to have been granted Mail.Read as an *application* permission,
  admin-consented in Azure AD (a console step, not something this code
  can do). Same never-raises contract as the Gmail fetch.

Both routers (gmail_provider.py, microsoft_graph_provider.py) now call
fetch -> normalize_*_message() -> process_channel_intake() for each
notification, the exact same pipeline /providers/email/webhook already
uses, and report per-message intake_status/document_kind/draft_object_type
in the response instead of just acknowledging.

Also fixed, found while reading this code: app/routers/drafts.py had NO
permission dependency on any of its 3 routes (list/read/publish an
extracted draft), unlike every comparable Core-facing router in this
codebase (resume_builder.py, jobs.py both gate via
Depends(require_permission(...))). Added drafts:read/drafts:publish,
matching the established pattern. RBAC_ENFORCEMENT defaults to disabled,
so this is a no-op until an operator enables it and grants those
permissions to whichever token Core uses.

Verified: all 3 pre-existing HERMES-850 scripts still pass unchanged (10
+ 6 + 9 checks). App imports cleanly, 110 routes registered (was 106
before this commit's additions). New scripts/hermes-850-live-fetch-check.py
(7 checks, mocked urllib.request.urlopen) verifies request shapes, cursor
handling, and error-swallowing -- explicitly NOT a live-credentials test,
since no HERMES_GMAIL_*/HERMES_MS_GRAPH_* credentials exist in this
environment. A real end-to-end pass against an actual Gmail/Graph mailbox
is still required once those OAuth apps are registered and credentials
are supplied.

feat(drafts): add reject_draft_object, mirroring publish

Needed by Core's draft-review workflow: a reviewer needs a way to
dismiss a draft that doesn't warrant creating a real Core record (e.g.
a hotlist or profile draft, since Core-side auto-creation of those was
explicitly scoped out) without leaving it stuck in a pending-forever
state. DraftStatus already had "rejected" as a valid value in
app/drafts/models.py; nothing previously set it.

POST /drafts/{draft_id}/reject accepts an optional {reason: string},
stored in the draft's metadata, and emits a draft.rejected event
alongside the existing draft.created/draft.published ones. Same
drafts:publish permission as the publish route -- rejecting is the same
class of reviewer action as publishing, not a lesser one.
